Cyanophycin granule protein (CGP) is a promising protein for use as a food supplement and for the treatment of malnutrition.
Cyanophycin (CGP) is a biopolymer consisting of L‐arginine and aspartic acid.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of the nutritional value and possible therapeutic use of cyanophycin: (1) the degradation of cyanophycin by gut flora, (2) the degradation of CGP dipeptides by gut flora, and (3) the effect of cyanophycin‐containing food on the intestinal flora of mammals and birds.

the degradation of CGP and its dipeptide, L‐arginyl‐L‐aspartate, by bacteria from the digestive tracts of animals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CGP is susceptible to degradation in the digestive tracts of all mammals, fish and birds tested, with the exception of pigs, chickens and fish.
CGP is not a suitable feed additive, but that the degradation product arginyl aspartic acid (ADA) is a promising feed additive.
CGP is not susceptible to degradation by the gut flora.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degradation of CGP and cyanophycin (CGP‐CPY) is not a major concern for the use of these polymers in nutrition or therapy.
the degradation of CGP and the dipeptides is a complex issue.
CGP and its dipeptide are resistant to degradation by mammalian, avain and fish gut flora, but that they are susceptible to degradation by the gut flora of ruminants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CGP is susceptible to degradation by the gut flora of mammals, birds, and fish.
CGP is susceptible to bacterial degradation in the digestive tract of all animals studied.
the gut microbiota is a potential source of enzymes that degrade cyanophycin.
